title: Use of cross-reactivity immunoassay to orient insulin replacement in diabetic patients with high levels of insulin antibodies
author: Cardoso Landaburu, Pomares, et al.

steps.title: Prepare 125I‑A14 insulin tracer
steps.instruction: Obtain preservative‑free recombinant human insulin (Humulin C, Eli Lilly) and purify on a Sephadex G25 column (Amersham Biosciences). Label the insulin with 125I following Linde et al. and purify the labeled product by HPLC as described by Jørgensen et al. Aim for a specific radioactivity of 300–380 µCi/µg; the fresh tracer should have a specific activity of 380 µCi/µg, a calculated concentration of 5.8 × 10⁻¹¹ M (derived from 20 000 cpm), a relative mass of 5808 Da, and be used in a final incubation volume of 0.12 mL. Record the gamma‑counter efficiency (70 %).

steps.title: Set up RBA binding mixture
steps.instruction: For each serum sample prepare duplicate tubes containing 30 µL of serum and add 90 µL of assay buffer (0.1 M phosphate, 0.25 % non‑specific gamma globulin, 0.5 % bovine serum albumin, pH 7.4) that already contains 20 000 cpm of the 125I‑A14 insulin tracer. Incubate the tubes for 1 day at 4 °C. In parallel, prepare duplicate control tubes for each serum by adding excess unlabeled human insulin to a final concentration of 7.5 × 10⁻⁶ M to assess non‑specific binding.

substeps.instruction: Prepare assay buffer with the specified components and pH.
Add tracer to the buffer to achieve 20 000 cpm per tube.
Aliquot 30 µL serum into each tube and mix with 90 µL buffer‑tracer solution.
For non‑specific binding controls, add unlabeled insulin to reach 7.5 × 10⁻⁶ M.
Incubate all tubes for 24 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Precipitate and separate bound insulin
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 14 % polyethylene glycol 6000 (PEG‑6000) prepared in veronal buffer (0.05 M sodium barbital, 0.01 % Tween 20, pH 8.6) to each incubation tube, mix thoroughly, and allow the precipitate to form. Separate the precipitated (bound) fraction by centrifugation (conditions as per standard laboratory practice) and keep the pellet for radioactivity counting.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 14 % PEG‑6000 solution in the specified veronal buffer.
Add 1 mL of this solution to each tube.
Mix and let the precipitate develop.
Centrifuge to collect the pellet.

steps.title: Calculate specific binding percentage
steps.instruction: Count the radioactivity of each pellet with a gamma counter (efficiency 70 %). Compute the specific binding percentage as B% = Bwi% − Bie%, where Bwi% is the binding obtained without cold insulin and Bie% is the binding obtained with excess cold insulin. Use the mean + 3 SD of 30 normal human sera (≈ 4 %) as the assay cutoff for positivity.

substeps.instruction: Measure counts for each pellet.
Convert counts to percentage of total added tracer.
Subtract non‑specific binding (Bie%) from total binding (Bwi%) to obtain B%.
Compare B% to the cutoff (~4 %).

steps.title: Perform displacement RIA
steps.instruction: Prepare duplicate tubes with 30 µL of the patient’s serum and add ~20 000 cpm of the 125I‑A14 insulin tracer. Incubate for 5 days at 4 °C. In parallel, set up duplicate displacement tubes for each competitor (unlabeled regular human insulin, Detemir, Glargine, Glulisine, Lispro) using a concentration series ranging from 1 × 10⁻⁹ M to 1 × 10⁻⁶ M. Add the appropriate competitor concentration to each tube and continue the 5‑day incubation at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Prepare tracer‑serum mixture as described.
Create dilution series of each unlabeled insulin (1 × 10⁻⁹ M to 1 × 10⁻⁶ M).
Add each competitor dilution to duplicate tubes containing the tracer‑serum mixture.
Incubate all tubes for 5 days at 4 °C.

steps.title: Separate bound tracer in RIA
steps.instruction: After the 5‑day incubation, add 1 mL of the same 14 % PEG‑6000/veronal buffer solution to each tube, mix, and precipitate the bound tracer as in the RBA. Centrifuge and retain the pellet for gamma‑counting.

substeps.instruction: Add PEG‑6000 solution to each tube.
Mix and allow precipitation.
Centrifuge and collect the pellet.

steps.title: Determine affinity constants and selectivity
steps.instruction: Count the radioactivity of each pellet, calculate the bound/free (B/F) ratio for each competitor concentration, and plot B/F versus competitor concentration. Interpolate the concentration that gives 50 % of maximal displacement [(B/F)₀/2] to obtain the median affinity constant K₀ for each ligand. Verify that the tracer concentration (5.8 × 10⁻¹¹ M) is well below the inverse of K₀ (satisfied for K₀ = 10⁶–10⁸ M⁻¹). Compute the selectivity ratio Sᵢ = K_L / K_Cᵢ for each analog relative to the original insulin ligand.

substeps.instruction: Convert pellet counts to bound tracer amount.
Calculate free tracer (F) using F = C / (1 + B/F).
Generate B/F vs. competitor concentration curves.
Determine K₀ from the 50 % displacement point.
Calculate selectivity Sᵢ = K_L / K_Cᵢ.
